This function is called AFTER SVM prediction to correct hard cases.
Parameters:
    svm_prob : float  — P(y=1) from SVM (already sigmoid of decision score)
    features : dict   — raw feature dict with all 41 feature values

Returns:
    -1  : do not override SVM (rule not triggered)
    0   : override → predict NO (not feasible)
    1   : override → predict YES (feasible)
'''

def apply_rule_patch(svm_prob: float, features: dict) -> int:
    # ─── Extract key features ────────────────────────────────────────────
    sku_counts = features.get('sku_counts', 0)
    fill_ratio = features.get('fill_ratio', 0)
    spare_cap = features.get('spare_capacity', 0)
    sku_length_var = features.get('sku_length_var', 0)
    sku_average_volume = features.get('sku_average_volume', 0)
    wl_to_vehicle_wl_total = features.get('wl_to_vehicle_wl_total', 0)
    max_asr = features.get('max_asr', 1.0)
    sku_std_length = features.get('sku_std_length', 0)
    
    # ─── FN Correction: SVM under-confident (predicts NO, should be YES) ───
    # Pattern from hard cases: moderate fill_ratio (5000-7000), 
    # decent spare_capacity (~9000), medium sku_counts (~11), low SVM prob (0.17-0.25)
    # SVM over-weights sku_counts negative impact, misses that spare capacity is sufficient
    if svm_prob < 0.45:
        # Moderate fill ratio with positive spare capacity suggests feasible
        if spare_cap > 7500 and 9 <= sku_counts <= 13 and fill_ratio < 11000:
            # Additional check: not too much length variance (easier to pack)
            if sku_length_var < 55 and sku_average_volume < 3500:
                return 1  # Override to YES
    
    # ─── FP Correction: SVM over-confident (predicts YES, should be NO) ───
    # Pattern from hard cases: high fill_ratio (18000-21000), 
    # lower sku_counts (7-8), high length variance (~48), very high SVM prob (0.97-0.99)
    # High fill_ratio + high length variance = packing difficulty despite spare capacity
    if svm_prob > 0.85:
        # High fill ratio with high length variance indicates packing difficulty
        if fill_ratio > 14000 and sku_length_var > 42:
            # Lower sku_counts with high fill_ratio means larger individual items
            if sku_counts <= 9 and sku_average_volume > 2800:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    # ─── Additional FP pattern: high aspect ratio items are hard to pack ───
    # Even with good SVM score, very high aspect ratio items cause packing failures
    if svm_prob > 0.80:
        if max_asr > 6.5 and fill_ratio > 12000:
            # High aspect ratio + moderate-high fill = likely infeasible
            if sku_std_length > 7.0:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    return -1

    # ─── Extract key features ────────────────────────────────────────────
    sku_counts = features.get('sku_counts', 0)
    fill_ratio = features.get('fill_ratio', 0)
    spare_cap = features.get('spare_capacity', 0)
    sku_length_var = features.get('sku_length_var', 0)
    sku_average_volume = features.get('sku_average_volume', 0)
    max_asr = features.get('max_asr', 1.0)
    sku_std_length = features.get('sku_std_length', 0)
    sku_width_var = features.get('sku_width_var', 0)
    wl_to_vehicle_wl_total = features.get('wl_to_vehicle_wl_total', 0)
    
    # ─── FN Correction: SVM under-confident (predicts NO, should be YES) ───
    # Pattern: Good spare capacity but SVM over-weights sku_counts negative impact
    # Typical FN: sku_counts=11, fill_ratio=5000-7000, spare_cap~9000, prob=0.17-0.25
    # Geometric justification: Moderate item count with ample spare space = packable
    if svm_prob < 0.38:
        # Must have genuinely good spare capacity (above p25 threshold)
        if spare_cap > 8500 and 9 <= sku_counts <= 13:
            # Moderate fill ratio (not too dense)
            if fill_ratio < 9000:
                # Low-moderate length variance (items similar in length = easier packing)
                if sku_length_var < 52 and sku_average_volume < 3400:
                    return 1  # Override to YES
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 1: High fill + few large items + high variance ───
    # Pattern: High fill_ratio with fewer but larger items creates packing gaps
    # Typical FP: sku_counts=7-8, fill_ratio=18000-21000, length_var~48, prob=0.97-0.99
    # Geometric justification: Large items with high size variance leave unusable gaps
    if svm_prob > 0.72:
        if fill_ratio > 16000 and sku_counts <= 8:
            # High length variance means items don't nest well
            if sku_length_var > 46 and sku_average_volume > 3100:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 2: High aspect ratio items ────────────────────
    # Very elongated items (max_asr > 6) are hard to pack efficiently
    # Combined with moderate-high fill, creates infeasible configurations
    if svm_prob > 0.75:
        if max_asr > 6.2 and fill_ratio > 13000:
            # High std in length compounds the aspect ratio problem
            if sku_std_length > 7.0 and sku_width_var > 8.0:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 3: Extreme fill with dimension variance ───────
    # When fill is very high AND both length and width vary significantly,
    # packing becomes geometrically constrained despite volume availability
    if svm_prob > 0.80:
        if fill_ratio > 18000:
            if sku_length_var > 50 or (sku_length_var > 40 and sku_width_var > 9.0):
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    return -1

    1   : override → predict YES (feasible)

    # ─── Extract key features ────────────────────────────────────────────
    sku_counts = features.get('sku_counts', 0)
    spare_cap = features.get('spare_capacity', 0)
    sku_average_volume = features.get('sku_average_volume', 0)
    sku_length_var = features.get('sku_length_var', 0)
    sku_width_var = features.get('sku_width_var', 0)
    sku_std_length = features.get('sku_std_length', 0)
    max_asr = features.get('max_asr', 1.0)
    
    # Derived fill ratio from spare_capacity and typical vehicle volume
    # Vehicle volume = 60 * 25 * 30 = 45000
    vehicle_volume = 45000
    fill_ratio = vehicle_volume - spare_cap if spare_cap < vehicle_volume else 0
    
    # ─── FN Correction: SVM under-confident (predicts NO, should be YES) ───
    # Pattern: Moderate item count with decent spare capacity but SVM over-penalizes
    # Typical FN: sku_counts=11, spare_cap~9000, moderate volume items
    # Geometric: Similar-sized items (low variance) pack efficiently despite count
    if svm_prob < 0.45:
        # Moderate spare capacity (above FN mean ~9240 but not extreme)
        if 7500 <= spare_cap <= 14000:
            # Moderate item count (FN typical: 11 items)
            if 9 <= sku_counts <= 13:
                # Items not too large on average (below p75 of ~3198)
                if sku_average_volume < 3350:
                    # Low-moderate length variance enables efficient packing
                    if sku_length_var < 55:
                        return 1  # Override to YES
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 1: High fill + few large items + high variance ───
    # Pattern: Few but large items with high size variance create unusable gaps
    # Typical FP: sku_counts=7-8, fill_ratio=18000-21000, length_var~48
    # Geometric: Large items with varying dimensions leave awkward voids
    if svm_prob > 0.65:
        if fill_ratio > 17000 and sku_counts <= 8:
            # High length variance means items don't nest/stack well
            if sku_length_var > 44 and sku_average_volume > 3000:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 2: High aspect ratio + high fill ────────────
    # Very elongated items (max_asr > 6) are geometrically difficult
    # Combined with high fill, creates infeasible configurations
    if svm_prob > 0.70:
        if max_asr > 6.0 and fill_ratio > 15000:
            # High std in length compounds aspect ratio packing difficulty
            if sku_std_length > 6.5:
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    # ─── FP Correction Pattern 3: Extreme fill with dimension variance ─────
    # When fill is very high AND both length and width vary significantly,
    # packing becomes geometrically constrained despite volume availability
    if svm_prob > 0.75:
        if fill_ratio > 18500:
            # High variance in multiple dimensions = poor nesting
            if sku_length_var > 48 or (sku_length_var > 40 and sku_width_var > 8.5):
                return 0  # Override to NO
    
    return -1
